title: CTS 2026 Weekly Survey 1 - Divorce and Remarriage

field_dates.final_close_rule: 21 days after the first production invitation send
field_dates.date_note: Week 1 launched outside the normal Tuesday cadence; this is the scheduled three-week final close target from the first Week 1 production invitation window.

suggestion_columns: Suggest one or more future CTS survey items. Please write each suggestion as a statement that a participant could rate from 0 to 100.

source_columns: Q1
In ordinary cases, a spouse's sexual adultery constitutes biblically legitimate grounds for divorce.
items.text: In ordinary cases, a spouse's sexual adultery constitutes biblically legitimate grounds for divorce.

source_columns: Q2
In ordinary cases, a spouse's persistent physical abuse constitutes biblically legitimate grounds for divorce even if sexual adultery has not occurred.
items.text: In ordinary cases, a spouse's persistent physical abuse constitutes biblically legitimate grounds for divorce even if sexual adultery has not occurred.

source_columns: Q3
In ordinary cases, a spouse's severe and persistent emotional or psychological abuse can constitute biblically legitimate grounds for divorce.
items.text: In ordinary cases, a spouse's severe and persistent emotional or psychological abuse can constitute biblically legitimate grounds for divorce.

source_columns: Q4
In ordinary cases, willful abandonment by an unbelieving spouse constitutes biblically legitimate grounds for divorce.
items.text: In ordinary cases, willful abandonment by an unbelieving spouse constitutes biblically legitimate grounds for divorce.

source_columns: Q5
In ordinary cases, a spouse's persistent pornography use can become biblically legitimate grounds for divorce.
items.text: In ordinary cases, a spouse's persistent pornography use can become biblically legitimate grounds for divorce.

source_columns: Q6
In ordinary cases, a spouse's romantic but nonsexual infidelity can constitute biblically legitimate grounds for divorce.
items.text: In ordinary cases, a spouse's romantic but nonsexual infidelity can constitute biblically legitimate grounds for divorce.

source_columns: Q7
A Christian whose divorce was biblically legitimate is normally free to remarry.
items.text: A Christian whose divorce was biblically legitimate is normally free to remarry.

source_columns: Q8
Churches should normally require pastoral review before affirming the remarriage of a divorced Christian.
items.text: Churches should normally require pastoral review before affirming the remarriage of a divorced Christian.

source_columns: Q9
Churches should use formal discipline when members knowingly pursue a biblically illegitimate divorce.
items.text: Churches should use formal discipline when members knowingly pursue a biblically illegitimate divorce.

source_columns: In my ministry context, churches are generally too permissive about divorce and remarriage.
items.text: In my ministry context, churches are generally too permissive about divorce and remarriage.

source_columns: Churches should treat immediate physical safety as a priority before pursuing marital reconciliation in abusive marriages.
items.text: Churches should treat immediate physical safety as a priority before pursuing marital reconciliation in abusive marriages.

source_columns: Pastors should distinguish carefully between ordinary marital conflict and patterns of coercive control when counseling about divorce.
items.text: Pastors should distinguish carefully between ordinary marital conflict and patterns of coercive control when counseling about divorce.

source_columns: Pastors should sometimes name specific political movements or parties when warning a congregation about moral compromise.
items.text: Pastors should sometimes name specific political movements or parties when warning a congregation about moral compromise.

source_columns: Churches should encourage regular fasting as a normal expectation for mature Christian discipleship.
items.text: Churches should encourage regular fasting as a normal expectation for mature Christian discipleship.

source_columns: Churches should avoid using worship songs from ministries whose leaders teach serious doctrinal error, even when the songs themselves are orthodox.
items.text: Churches should avoid using worship songs from ministries whose leaders teach serious doctrinal error, even when the songs themselves are orthodox.
